page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, it features 16 physical cores with single-threading, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs. The architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache, and a 36 MB shared L3 cache, along with hardware AES encryption support. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and comes bundled with 950 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

In performance evaluations, the c8gd.4xlarge demonstrates exceptional memory throughput, ranking in the top tier for PassMark memory benchmarks alongside strong uncached read and write bandwidths of 296.81 GB/sec and 124.13 GB/sec. CPU benchmarks such as Geekbench and stress-ng exhibit solid mid-range multi-core processing performance. Database operations and multi-threaded decompression tests score in the upper quartile. However, the system demonstrates lower relative throughput in larger language model prompt processing due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware acceleration and vector-heavy instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX.

The resource profile makes the c8gd.4xlarge cost-efficient for compute-intensive tasks requiring high-speed local temporary storage and strong memory bandwidth. Optimal deployment scenarios include high-performance relational and NoSQL databases, software compilation, batch processing, data transformation pipelines, and static web serving workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by a 16-core 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs with 1:1 physical core mapping, 32.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), and a bundled 950 GB local NVMe SSD drive alongside 8 Gbps network bandwidth. Memory performance is a primary benchmark highlight, showing top-tier bandwidth and strong multi-threaded decompression efficiency. While general CPU scores fall in the middle tier and LLM inference is limited without discrete GPU acceleration, database operations perform in the upper quartile. The instance delivers solid cost efficiency for compute-focused workloads that benefit from direct NVMe storage, such as database servers, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web serving, and ETL data processing.
